thread.title: Earnings Season Nears Halfway Point: About 80% of S&P Companies Tally Beats

author: thestreet.com
title: Earnings Season Nears Halfway Point: About 80% of S&P Companies Tally Beats
text:
As earnings season nears the halfway point, companies that already have reported illustrated a strong end to last year.
According to data from S&P Dow Jones Indices, 201 companies on the S&P 500 Index have reported fourth-quarter earnings, totaling 49.5% of the market value and about 40% of the index's constituents.
Of those that have reported, 159 have beaten earnings estimates, 23 have missed estimates and 19 have been in line with estimates. Of the 200 companies with full compatible reporting, 157, or 78.5%, have beaten Wall Street's sales estimates.
Financials have beaten earnings estimates on 36 of the sector's 43 releases so far, or 83.7%. The sector rallied 6.4% in January.
Information technology companies also have performed well this earnings season, as 30 of the 34 companies that have reported, or 88.2%, have beaten Wall Street's forecasts. That sector was up 7.6% for January.
The healthcare sector gained 6.6% in January after 21 of the 23 companies that have reported, or 91.3%, beat earnings estimates.
Overall fourth-quarter GAAP earnings have declined broadly by 15.5% as a result of write-downs related to tax reform that compounded regular fourth-quarter charges, S&P found. Tax-related charges totaled an estimated $41.3 billion.
"For 2018, company guidance has been positive, as most cite savings due to lower income taxes , with companies guiding higher, to which analysts followed," S&P said. "Typically at this time of year, full-year estimates decline, as analysts face reality and update their target prices, earnings and buy/sell/hold recommendations."
But for January 2018, operating estimates for the year have increased 5.1% and 2019 earnings estimates have been raised 5.9%.
"While (Wall) Street liked the higher numbers, and showed it in the prices, the question to determine is how much growth is due to income tax reduction and how much is from actual product growth and sales," S&P noted.
Stocks finished January strong, earning their best monthly performance since March 2016. By late-morning on the first trading day in February, stocks traded mixed ahead of earnings from Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) , Alphabet Inc. ( GOOGL ) and Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN ) .
